# Axis Bank FY25 Master Summary

Axis Bank delivered resilient financial performance in FY25 despite global economic headwinds, reporting consolidated net profit of ₹28,055 crores (6% YoY growth) and standalone net profit of ₹26,373 crores. Operating profit surged 13% to ₹42,105 crores, driven by operating revenue growth of 10% to ₹79,605 crores. Net Interest Income rose 9% to ₹54,348 crores, while non-interest income expanded 13% to ₹25,257 crores. However, profitability metrics moderated with RoA declining from 1.83% to 1.74% (consolidated: 1.77%) and RoE falling from 18.86% to 16.52% (consolidated: 16.89%), while EPS dropped from ₹80.67 to ₹71.37.

The balance sheet expanded robustly with total assets reaching ₹16.1 lakh crores (9% growth). Advances grew 8% to ₹10.4 lakh crores, with retail loans comprising 60% of the book (7% growth) and corporate loans rising 8%. High RAROC segments—Small Business Banking, SME, and Mid-Corporate—grew 14% YoY, now representing 23% of the loan book. Deposits increased 10% to ₹11.7 lakh crores, though CASA ratio declined 328 bps to 39.26%. Retail term deposits grew 8% and Burgundy Private AUM expanded 16%. Operating subsidiaries contributed ₹1,768 crores in combined PAT (11% growth) with 46% ROI.

Capital strength remained fortress-like with Capital Adequacy Ratio at 19.12%, Tier 1 at 16.47%, and CET-1 at 14.67% (up 93 bps YoY). The Bank maintained ₹11,957 crores in non-NPA provisions, though asset quality deteriorated with Gross NPA rising from 2.82% to 3.70% and Net NPA increasing from 0.73% to 1.05% (consolidated: 0.33%). Provisions surged 91% to ₹7,759 crores due to higher slippages. Provision Coverage Ratio declined from 75% to 72%, while Net Interest Margin compressed 9 bps to 3.98% as cost of funds rose 21 bps to 5.46%.

Strategic expansion continued aggressively with 5,879 branches across 3,194 cities (adding 500 branches), 13,941 ATMs, and 89% district coverage. Digital transformation accelerated with ~3 crore mobile banking customers generating 8.7 billion transactions (36% growth) and ₹25.7 trillion spends (20% growth). WhatsApp banking reached 30 million users.

Sustainability initiatives progressed significantly, with sustainable wholesale lending reaching ₹48,412 crores against the new ₹60,000 crore 2030 target. The Bank exceeded Mission 2 Million goals, impacting 2.05 million participants and planting 3.27 million trees. Women's workforce representation reached 27.7%, approaching the 30% fiscal 2027 target. Governance remained robust with 8 Independent Directors (85% with finance expertise) and India's first Board-level ESG Committee established in 2021.

# HDFC Bank FY25 Comprehensive Summary

HDFC Bank delivered resilient financial performance in FY25, completing its first full year following the landmark merger with HDFC Limited (effective July 1, 2023). The bank reported profit after tax of ₹67,347.4 crore, representing 10.7% year-on-year growth, with earnings per share reaching ₹88.3. Total income stood at ₹3,46,149.3 crore as the balance sheet expanded 8% to ₹39.10 lakh crore.

**Financial Metrics and Balance Sheet Management:** The bank strategically repositioned its balance sheet, achieving deposits of ₹27.15 lakh crore (14.1% growth) while moderating advances growth to 5.4%, reaching ₹26.20 lakh crore. This deliberate approach improved the credit-deposit ratio from 110% at merger to 96% and reduced high-cost borrowings to 14%. Net Interest Income grew 13.0% to ₹1,22,670.1 crore, with Net Interest Margin maintained at 3.48%. The cost-to-income ratio stood at 40.5%. Return on Average Assets was 1.91%, while Return on Equity declined slightly to 14.6% from 16.1%.

**Capital and Asset Quality:** The bank maintained robust capitalization with a Capital Adequacy Ratio of 19.6% (Tier 1: 17.7%), well above the regulatory minimum of 11.7%. Asset quality remained industry-leading, with Gross NPA at just 1.33% and Net NPA at 0.43%. The coverage ratio stood at 172.1%, including general and floating provisions. The Board proposed a dividend of ₹22.0 per share, representing a 25% payout ratio.

**Network and Digital Transformation:** Serving 9.7 crore customers, the bank operates through 24,854 banking outlets, including 9,455 branches (51% in semi-urban and rural areas), 21,139 ATMs, and 15,399 business correspondents across 4,150 cities. Digital transformation accelerated significantly, with 97% of financial transactions and 86% of acquisitions now digital, achieving 99.95% customer uptime. The bank captured 14.6% incremental deposit market share with only 5% branch market share, demonstrating exceptional franchise strength.

**Strategic Priorities and Risk Management:** Operating as a Domestic Systemically Important Bank (D-SIB), the bank follows an "Employee First, Customer First, Technology First, and Power of the Group" strategy. The workforce of 2,14,521 employees (26.14% women) received 1.25 crore learning hours, though attrition remained elevated at 22.60%. Risk management encompasses ten critical areas including credit, market, compliance, operational, climate, and cyber risks, with zero environmental and social non-compliance incidents reported.

**Sustainability and Outlook:** The bank invested ₹1,068.03 crore in CSR through its Parivartan program, impacting 10.56 crore lives cumulatively. Operating 2,507 green-certified branches, it achieved a 45% reduction in Scope 1&2 emission intensity, targeting carbon neutrality by FY32. Management expressed confidence in growing advances on par with the system in FY26 and exceeding it in FY27, supported by strengthened fundamentals despite global tariff uncertainties and geopolitical headwinds.

# ICICI Bank FY25 Annual Report: Master Summary

ICICI Bank delivered robust financial performance in FY2025, with profit after tax rising 15.5% to ₹472.27 billion from ₹408.88 billion in FY2024. Consolidated profit after tax reached ₹510.29 billion, up 15.3% year-on-year. Net interest income grew 9.2% to ₹811.65 billion, driven by 14.5% growth in average interest-earning assets, though net interest margin compressed 21 basis points to 4.32% due to rising funding costs. Fee income expanded 14.8% to ₹238.70 billion, while core operating profit jumped 12.5% to ₹653.96 billion. Operating expenses increased 8.3% to ₹423.72 billion, improving the cost-to-income ratio to 38.63% from 40.23%. The Board recommended a dividend of ₹11.00 per equity share.

The bank's balance sheet demonstrated strong growth with total assets expanding 13.2% to ₹21,182.40 billion. Net advances grew 13.3% to ₹13,417.66 billion, with domestic advances up 13.9%, while deposits increased 14.0% to ₹16,103.48 billion. The Business Banking portfolio serving enterprises with turnover up to ₹7.50 billion grew 33.7% to ₹2,633.67 billion, contributing 19.6% of net advances. However, the CASA ratio moderated to 39.0% from 40.4% as term deposit costs increased 43 basis points to 6.65%, driving overall cost of funds up 24 basis points to 5.10%.

Asset quality remained healthy with gross NPA ratio stable at 0.4% and net NPA ratio improving to 0.39% from 0.42%. The corporate portfolio maintained strong credit quality with 74.8% rated A- and above. However, provisions increased significantly by 28.5% to ₹46.83 billion due to higher NPA additions in retail and rural segments, while provision coverage ratio declined to 76.2% from 80.3%. Capital adequacy remained robust with total CAR at 16.55%, Tier-1 at 15.94%, and CET-1 at 15.94%, all comfortably above regulatory requirements. Consolidated return on equity stood at 18.0%.

A landmark corporate action was the merger of ICICI Securities, which became effective March 24, 2025, resulting in the entity becoming a wholly-owned subsidiary following delisting. The bank issued 56 million equity shares to public shareholders under the approved swap ratio. Total equity shares outstanding reached 7.12 billion, with foreign institutional investors holding the largest stake at 37.30%.

The bank pursued aggressive digital expansion with its iMobile app processing 558 million transactions worth ₹11,238 billion, while maintaining physical presence across 6,983 branches and 16,285 ATMs. On sustainability, ICICI Bank set a carbon neutrality target for Scope 1 and 2 emissions by FY2032, with sustainable finance portfolio reaching ₹906 billion. CSR spending totaled ₹8.01 billion, including a commitment of ₹18.00 billion for cancer care facilities. Key risks include sensitivity to interest rate movements with 53.5% of domestic loans linked to external benchmarks, regulatory changes, and market volatility.

# Kotak Mahindra Bank FY25 Master Summary

Kotak Mahindra Bank delivered strong financial performance in FY25, with consolidated net profit reaching ₹22,126 crore, representing 21.5% growth from ₹18,213 crore in FY24. This performance was significantly boosted by a ₹3,013 crore gain from divesting its 70% stake in Kotak Mahindra General Insurance to Zurich Insurance for ₹4,095.82 crore. Standalone bank net profit grew to ₹16,450 crore from ₹13,782 crore. The Group's total assets expanded 14.5% to ₹8.8 trillion with a four-year CAGR of 16%, serving 5.3 crore customers (6% YoY growth) through 2,148 bank branches and 3,295 ATMs across India, employing over 114,000 people.

**Key Financial Metrics:** Bank advances grew 18% (four-year CAGR) to ₹4,86,166 crore, while deposits increased 11.2% to ₹4,99,055 crore with a robust 16% CAGR. However, the CASA ratio declined significantly from 52.8% to 45.5%, as term deposits grew at an exceptional 28% CAGR to ₹2,84,639 crore, pressuring funding costs. Net interest income reached ₹37,394 crore (17% CAGR), though Net Interest Margin compressed from 5.3% to 5.0%. Capital and reserves strengthened to ₹1,57,395 crore (17% CAGR), supporting a robust Capital Adequacy Ratio of 23.3% (CET1: 22.3%, Tier I: 21.1%), well above regulatory requirements. The Liquidity Coverage Ratio stood at 135.46% and Net Stable Funding Ratio at 115.71%.

**Asset Quality & Profitability:** Asset quality remained excellent with Gross NPA ratio at 1.4% and Net NPA ratio at 0.31%, down from 1.21% in FY21. Return on Equity stood at 15.2% with ROA at 2.7%. Earnings per share increased to ₹111.29 from ₹91.45, while book value per share rose 21% to ₹792 from ₹653. Market capitalization reached ₹4.3 trillion with share price at ₹2,171.

**Business Performance:** The diversified model demonstrated strength across segments. Asset Management grew AAUM 35% YoY to ₹468,820 crore (7.09% market share). Investment Banking maintained #1 ranking in India ECM for three consecutive years, executing 31 transactions including 18 IPOs. Kotak Securities achieved 11.6% market share with PAT of ₹1,640 crore. Life Insurance reported ₹15,320 crore gross written premium with 25% VNB margin. The Kotak811 platform serves 2.56 crore savings accounts with 35% growth in throughput and 28% reduction in net customer complaints.

**Strategic Challenges & Initiatives:** The bank faced regulatory headwinds when RBI imposed an embargo in April 2024 on digital customer onboarding and credit card issuance due to IT examination deficiencies, lifted in February 2025. The bank responded with comprehensive gap assessments, upgraded policies, established the IT Risk and Information Security Committee (IRISC), and deployed SOAR solutions, achieving ISO/IEC 27001 certification. The microcredit business experienced industry-wide stress requiring underwriting adjustments. The bank is executing a multi-year transformation targeting 1.5-2x nominal GDP growth with enhanced digital platforms and strong ESG commitments, including ₹999 crore in green finance and ₹389.3 crore CSR expenditure.

# SBI FY25 Annual Report: Master Summary

State Bank of India delivered exceptional financial performance in FY25, with standalone net profit surging 16.08% year-on-year to ₹70,901 crore, marking its strongest profitability yet. Operating profit crossed the milestone ₹1 lakh crore mark for the first time, reaching ₹1.11 lakh crore with 17.89% growth. The bank's balance sheet expanded to ₹66.76 lakh crore, maintaining dominant market positions of 22.54% in deposits and 19.36% in advances.

**Financial Performance Highlights:** Net Interest Income grew 4.43% to ₹1.67 lakh crore, while fee income increased 9.93%. Total interest income rose 11.41% to ₹4.62 lakh crore, though interest expenses increased faster at 15.78% to ₹2.96 lakh crore. Return on Assets improved to 1.10% from 1.04%, with earnings per share reaching ₹79.44. The board declared a dividend of ₹15.90 per share. The cost-to-income ratio improved significantly to 51.64% from 55.66%.

**Balance Sheet Strength:** Deposits grew 9.48% with CASA ratio at 39.97%, while current account deposits surged 27.02%. Net advances increased robustly by 12.40% to ₹41.63 lakh crore, with domestic credit-deposit ratio improving to 69.71%. Key segment performances included SME portfolio crossing ₹5 lakh crore (16.86% growth), home loans reaching ₹8.31 lakh crore, and agricultural lending at ₹3.49 lakh crore.

**Asset Quality Transformation:** Gross NPA declined 42 basis points to 1.82%, with net NPA at an impressive 0.47%, down from 0.57%. Provision Coverage Ratio stood strong at 74.42% (92.08% including AUCA). The bank recovered through multiple channels including 1,208 NCLT cases, with 272 resolution plans approved. Credit risk-weighted assets to gross advances improved 107 basis points to 58.07%.

**Capital Position:** Capital adequacy reached robust levels with CET1 ratio at historic high of 10.81% and overall CAR at 14.25%, comfortably exceeding regulatory requirements. As a D-SIB, SBI maintains additional CET1 capital requirements of 0.80% from April 2025. The bank maintains top credit ratings: Moody's Baa3/Stable, S&P BBB-/Positive, and Fitch BBB-/Stable, with domestic instruments rated AAA/Stable.

**Strategic Initiatives:** SBI operates 22,937 branches and 63,791 ATMs serving 520 million customers, with YONO platform reaching 87.7 million registered users. The bank targets 7.5% green portfolio by 2030, supported by $3.07 billion from DFIs/MDBs and ₹1,050 million through green bonds. Infrastructure includes over 31 MW solar capacity, 61 IGBC-certified buildings, and 542 rainwater harvesting systems. CSR expenditure reached ₹610.77 crore across 1,408 activities benefiting 65 lakh+ people.
